To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formation of uranyl carbonato ternary complexes inhibits the rate of U(VI)-reducing bacterial metabolism.
the presence of Ca2+ in the influent water decreases the rate of U(VI)-reducing bacteria Shewanella putrifaciens reduction of U(VII).

(1) the presence of calcium ions in the influent stream inhibits the biological reduction of uranium in a packed column of ferrihydryte-coated sand, (2) uranium is transported in the influent and effluent stream as a Ca-UO2-carbonato complex, and (3) uranium is transported as a Ca-U-carbonato complex in the effluent stream when the influent is calcium free.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of radionuclides within the vadose zone, with a specific focus on the influence of uranyl complexation on its transport within a subsurface environment.
the transport and fate of U(VI)-containing contaminants through subsurface systems.
the fate of uranium (U) in groundwater.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of ternery Ca-UO2 complexes in the presence of ferrihyrite coated sand results in the complete inhibition of uranyl reduction.
the presence of calcium in the influent water will inhibit the reduction of uranium by Shewanella.
uranyl reduction by S. putrefaciens in ferrihydride coated sand is highly dependent upon the uranyl speciation and the formation of ternaries complexes, which are favored in the presence of Ca.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of uranyl reduction by S. putrefaciens is inversely related to the concentration of Ca2+.
the presence of Ca, and the resultant formation of uranyl carbonate complexes, inhibits U(VI) transport by decreasing the rate of reduction.
uranyl speciation, in particular the presence of Ca, is a critical factor in controlling the rate and extent of microbial U(VI) dissimilation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
uranyl reduction by S. putrefaciens is not only influenced by competing electron donors but also by uranyl speciation and the mineralogical matrix.
the presence of Ca in solution can inhibit U(VI) transport and retard the rate of U(VI)-reducing bacterial activity.
